title: Telemetry-driven canary for mixed-precision quant rollouts
creator: Samir Khatri
description:
Goal: Build a telemetry-first canary and rollback mechanism to safely publish mixed-precision quantization profiles (INT8 / GPTQ / AWQ / experimental FP8) and pin model versions in the model catalog. The flow should allow progressive rollouts with automatic guardrails based on accuracy regressions, cost/latency deltas, and customer-visible error signals.

Background: We currently publish quant profiles as part of the model catalog but rely on manual QA and ad-hoc smoke tests. Several regressions slipped into serving when a profile reduced quality for long-context chat workloads and for reranking models. We need an end-to-end plan that ties: 1) canonical telemetry fields emitted by the runtime, 2) an automated canary release policy in the control plane, and 3) a deterministic rollback path with alerts and audit logs.

Scope:
- Define telemetry schema additions to capture: quant_family, quant_bits, kernel_variant, kv_cache_hit_rate, per_token_latency_p95, prompt_length_bucket, model_variant_pinned_version, and cheap quality proxies (e.g., FMAP / rerank delta / embedding cosine drift).
- Implement runtime tags/fields and ensure the private control plane ingests them into the observability pipeline.
- Add canary release orchestration in the rollout service: staged percentages, time windows, automatic promotion/rollback based on thresholds.
- Wire automated regression detection to the alerting system and to a one-click rollback that pins the catalog to previous working profile.
- Publish process & runbook for on-call and SEs.

Out of scope (for this ticket): creating new heavy-weight human Evals; full model re-training. Those are follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry schema merged and runtime emits new fields for all quantified models in staging
Canary orchestration supports staged traffic splits (e.g., 1%, 10%, 50%) with configurable wait windows
Automatic rollback triggers on any of: quality proxy regression > 4% absolute, per-token latency p95 increase > 25%, token cost delta > 15% without quality improvement
Canary run results visible in Console canary dashboard with links to sample traces and failing prompts
One-click rollback pins model catalog/version to last-known-good profile and is audited in the release logs
